title: Annual general meeting (AGM) deadline
summary: Hold the annual general meeting that adopts the audited financial statements for the year. AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1 and MGT-15 deadlines run from this meeting.
applicability: Every company other than a One Person Company. First AGM within 9 months of the end of the first financial year; later AGMs within 6 months of the year end (30 September for a 31 March year end), with no more than 15 months between two AGMs. The ROC may extend a later AGM by up to 3 months on an application in Form GNL-1.
law: Section 96(1), Companies Act 2013; Section 99 (punishment); Section 101(1) (21 clear days' notice)
penalty: Section 99: the company and every officer in default are punishable with a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh and, for a continuing default, up to Rs 5,000 for every day the default continues (court-imposed fine).

other: Court-imposed fine on prosecution, not an adjudicated penalty
Tribunal can order the meeting on a member's application (Section 97)
exposure.basis: Section 99: fine up to Rs 1 lakh plus up to Rs 5,000 per day of continuing default; no overall cap on the daily amount

summary: File the adopted standalone financial statements (and consolidated statements, if any) with the Board's report and auditor's report. Since 14-07-2025 the V3 forms also need the linked e-forms Extract of Board Report and Extract of Auditor's Report.
applicability: Every company other than a One Person Company (see mca-aoc4-opc-annual). XBRL mode for listed companies and their Indian subsidiaries, companies with paid-up capital of Rs 5 crore or more or turnover of Rs 100 crore or more, and Ind AS companies (banking, insurance, NBFC and housing finance companies excluded). Ind AS NBFCs use AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS). Companies preparing consolidated statements also file AOC-4 CFS (or the consolidated XBRL / NBFC variant).

title: FLA return (foreign liabilities and assets)
authority: RBI (Department of Statistics and Information Management)
summary: Report foreign direct investment and overseas direct investment liabilities and assets as at end-March to RBI on the FLAIR portal by 15 July; unaudited figures are allowed and are revised after audit.
applicability: Indian companies and LLPs (and AIFs, partnership firms and others) that received FDI or made ODI in the previous year or the current year (April-March).
law: Regulation 4(2), FEM (Mode of Payment and Reporting of Non-Debt Instruments) Regulations 2019; Regulation 10(5), FEM (Overseas Investment) Regulations 2022; Master Direction - Reporting under FEMA
penalty: Late submission fee of Rs 7,500 (non-flow return). Non-filing is a FEMA contravention: Section 13 penalty up to Rs 2 lakh where the amount is not quantifiable plus up to Rs 5,000 per day; compounding guidance is Rs 10,000 per delayed FLA return.

other: Section 13 FEMA 1999: adjudicated penalty up to 3 times the sum involved (up to Rs 2 lakh where not quantifiable) plus up to Rs 5,000 per day of continuing contravention
Compounding guidance Rs 10,000 per delayed FLA return
